channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Por que a 3ª via não consegue eleger presidentes no Brasil. Entenda
item.description: The difficulty of a third-way candidacy in Brazilian presidential elections is not merely due to lack of votes, but to a combination of historical, partisan, and strategic factors that prevent the consolidation of alternatives outside the Lula-Bolsonaro polarization. Experts note that centrist parties have historically prioritized joining governments and negotiating power rather than building independent national projects, and that third-way candidacies are often poorly planned, launched too late, and lacking solid foundations. Despite a segment of the electorate that identifies with neither left nor right, this group rarely translates into sustained support for a competitive third-way candidate.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro busca votos para Roscoe, mas esbarra em Cleitinho
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro campaigned in Minas Gerais to boost Flávio Roscoe’s gubernatorial bid, aiming to link him to the Bolsonaro movement. However, he faces resistance due to the popularity of Senator Cleitinho Azevedo, who, despite supporting Bolsonaro for president, leads in polls and has strong conservative backing. The PL is relying on Nikolas Ferreira and additional visits to strengthen Roscoe’s position, but shifting votes from Cleitinho remains a major challenge.

item.title: Pesquisas internas de Lula e de Flávio apontam direções opostas
item.description: Internal polls from Lula's and Flávio Bolsonaro's campaigns show opposing scenarios: Lula's tracking indicates a 5-7 point lead, while Flávio's shows a technical tie. Official polls, including BTG/Nexus and Quaest, confirm a tight race with Lula ahead, though his lead has been shrinking over the past month.

item.title: Brasil tem menos transparência em anúncios nas redes sociais que União Europeia e Reino Unido, aponta estudo
item.description: A study by NetLab/UFRJ and the Minderoo Centre at the University of Cambridge found that Brazil offers less transparency in social media advertising than the European Union and the United Kingdom. On platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and X (formerly Twitter), access to advertising data is rated as insufficient, unavailable, or insignificant, making it harder to monitor the influence of money in political discourse, particularly during an election year.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad gastaram ao menos R$ 2,2 milhões em anúncios no Instagram e no Facebook em 2026, mesmo antes do início da campanha
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad spent at least R$ 2.2 million on Instagram and Facebook ads in 2026 before the official campaign period began, according to a g1 survey using Meta’s Ad Library data. Although these expenditures are not considered irregular by the TRE-SP, they are not counted toward campaign spending caps and were estimated using the minimum value of each ad spend range reported by the platform.

item.title: De minuta de contrato a almoço reservado: entenda as suspeitas da PF envolvendo a relação entre Lulinha, Roberta e Marcola
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating suspicions of influence peddling involving businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, lobbyist; Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula; and Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), former chief of staff to the president. Roberta is suspected of having sent Marcola a draft contract for the sale of cannabidiol to the Ministry of Health without bidding, linked to a deal with the 'INSS Careca', already arrested for diverting INSS funds. WhatsApp messages also show Roberta and Lulinha discussing business at 'another level', with future plans in Switzerland, while Marcola reportedly opposed the involvement of Fernando Bittar, Lulinha’s former business partner.

item.title: ¡Llamad a la primera dama!
item.description: Brazilian women will be decisive in the October 2026 presidential elections, yet the absence of female presidential candidates from major parties reveals the disconnect between party politics and national reality, where women lead nearly all social struggles while facing a rising tide of femicides.

item.title: MPE se manifesta a favor da elegibilidade de Deltan Dallagnol em 2026
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry (MPE) has expressed support for Deltan Dallagnol’s eligibility in the 2026 elections, stating that his 2021 resignation from the Federal Public Ministry (MPF) does not constitute a barrier to candidacy. The opinion notes that 13 of the 16 disciplinary proceedings underway at the time were later archived, and the three terminated by his resignation had no potential to result in dismissal, undermining the basis of the TSE’s 2023 decision that annulled his candidacy. The MPE also considers Dallagnol’s departure from the MPF as politically motivated, reinforcing the legitimacy of his Senate bid in Paraná.

item.title: Flávio toca um disco velho
item.description: Lula visited São Bernardo do Campo to evoke the historic 1979 strikes, aiming to align his campaign with Brazil’s labor movement legacy. Flávio Bolsonaro resumed an erratic discourse reminiscent of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, indicating an unpredictable electoral campaign steeped in nostalgic conservatism. The subscriber-exclusive article describes the onset of a polarized election defined by historical symbolism and renewed ideological confrontation.

item.title: Após estreia esvaziada no Rio, Flávio escala Nikolas, Tarcísio e Nunes para ampliar palanques em Minas e SP
item.description: After an underwhelming debut in Rio, Flávio Bolsonaro strengthened his campaign with events in Minas Gerais and São Paulo, relying on allies such as Nikolas Ferreira, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Ricardo Nunes to broaden his base. In Minas, he sought to balance support between the official PL candidate, Flávio Roscoe, and rival Cleitinho, aiming to turn internal division into national advantage. The strategy aims to solidify backing in Brazil’s two largest electoral colleges amid doubts about his mobilization capacity without Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Deus não vota, mas foi arrastado para os palanques de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: God was repeatedly invoked by the main presidential candidates in 2026, including Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, as a strategy to attract religious voters. The use of divine references in campaign speeches reflects the growing politicization of religion in Brazil, with both sides attempting to position themselves as defenders of Christian values, despite God not having a vote.

item.title: Michelle intensifica agenda com evangélicos enquanto rivais buscam espaço no segmento religioso no DF
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro is intensifying her Senate campaign in the Federal District with a focus on evangelical voters, attending religious events, singing alongside gospel artists, and meeting with leaders from Sara Nossa Terra. Her longstanding alignment with evangelical causes during the Bolsonaro government is being leveraged as a political asset, even as she campaigns for Flávio Bolsonaro for president amid local tensions with allies like Celina Leão.

item.title: STF pode retomar nesta quarta julgamento sobre eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) may resume on Wednesday the judgment on how to fill the Rio de Janeiro governorship after Cláudio Castro’s resignation, deciding whether the successor should be chosen by popular vote or indirectly by the State Legislative Assembly. The case stems from Castro’s ineligibility and the disqualification of others in the succession line, with the PSD alleging his resignation was a maneuver to keep the same political group in power. So far, four ministers have voted for indirect election, while Cristiano Zanin supported direct voting, leaving five ministers yet to vote.

item.title: Ministros do STF veem dificuldades para julgar mandato-tampão do Rio, mas caso segue na pauta
item.description: The STF is debating the interim mandate in Rio's government, but the scheduled Wednesday judgment remains uncertain due to possible agenda changes or requests for additional time. The case concerns succession after Governor Cláudio Castro's resignation, with a dispute between the Rio TJ President, Ricardo Couto, and the ALERJ President, Douglas Ruas, over who should govern until the January inauguration. So far, the vote was 4-1 in favor of indirect elections, though rapporteur Cristiano Zanin supports direct elections.

item.title: Caso Lulinha: as perguntas que devem ser feitas, para além da disputa política
item.description: The case involving Fábio Luís da Silva (Lulinha), son of President Lula, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger raises serious concerns about public ethics and conflicts of interest, with allegations of unregistered meetings, receipt of funds from companies tied to the INSS scandal, and direct financial transfers — including jewelry — to the Presidency’s chief of staff. Columnist Fernando Schüler argues this transcends left-right politics, revealing a deeper issue of patrimonialism in the Brazilian state, demanding a serious and swift investigation.

item.title: TSE reforma decisão e condena vereador por violência política de gênero no interior de MG
item.description: The TSE unanimously overturned the TRE-MG's acquittal and convicted councilman Ailson Batista de Figueiredo (MDB), known as 'Codó', of gender-based political violence. He was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months in prison and ordered to pay R$ 20,000 in damages after calling councilwoman Tatyana Figueiredo Navarro a 'whore' and 'slut' in a public speech, with remarks about her body and her sister. The ruling confirms his ineligibility for office.

item.title: PF suspeita que Roberta Luchsinger tinha autorização para agir em nome de Lulinha
item.description: The Federal Police states that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger appeared to have authorization to act on behalf of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, the eldest son of President Lula, based on messages in which she identified herself as him. The investigation, which led to three inquiries, examines suspected influence peddling involving the pair in federal government dealings with the Ministry of Health, Dataprev, and other administrative areas. The messages were obtained in a conversation with Gustavo Gaspar, former advisor to Senator Weverton Rocha, and are linked to Operation Sem Desconto, which investigates fraud in the INSS.

item.title: Ministros do TSE fazem reunião fechada sobre IA nas eleições, mas julgamento segue sem data marcada
item.description: TSE ministers held a closed-door meeting to discuss rules on AI use in campaigns and opinion polling, aiming to establish guidelines for the 2026 elections. Although the discussion was reported as calm and productive, no judgment date has been set by President Kassio Nunes Marques, despite pressure to rule this month. The issues divide the court, with a tendency to allow audiovisual resources in polls if disclosed to interviewees, while the use of AI avatars — such as the Bolsonaro video used by the PL — remains under review.

item.title: Nova pesquisa BTG/Nexus vai medir impacto da campanha na disputa Lula x Flávio
item.description: A new BTG/Nexus poll will be conducted from August 21 to 23, 2026, with results released on August 24, measuring voting intention and the impact of the electoral campaign in the presidential race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. The survey will also assess voter exposure to and identification with campaign materials, along with perceptions of Lula’s government, the economy, and electoral behavior. The sample size is 2,000 interviews, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Nova pesquisa mostra disputa Lula x Flávio em São Paulo
item.description: The Real Time Big Data poll will measure voting intentions in São Paulo for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, featuring a stimulated scenario with 13 candidates in the first round and a potential Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro runoff. Conducted between August 19–22 with 2,000 interviews, it will assess government approval, candidate rejection, and presidential performance perception, with results released on August 24.

item.title: TSE aceita desistência do PT em ação sobre Fundo Eleitoral e libera R$ 2,3 bilhões aos partidos
item.description: The TSE accepted the PT's withdrawal from a lawsuit challenging the distribution of the Electoral Fund, allowing the release of R$ 2.3 billion to parties. The unanimous decision maintained the seat calculation based on the PT's 68 deputies elected in 2022. The PL will receive the largest share (R$ 881.7 million), followed by the PT (R$ 615.4 million) and União Brasil (R$ 526.2 million).

item.title: Caiado critica Lula por zerar “taxa das blusinhas” em ano eleitoral
item.description: Presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized the Lula government's decision to eliminate the 'blusinhas tax' on international purchases under $50 during an election year, accusing it of bad faith and 'kleptocracy'. Caiado did not state whether he would maintain the zero rate or reinstate the 20% tariff, saying he would consult all sectors of society before deciding. He labeled the move opportunistic, criminal, and disrespectful to the Brazilian people.

item.title: Caiado: O Bolsa Família será mantido, é política de Estado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD candidate for president, stated that the Bolsa Família program will be maintained as state policy if he is elected. He made the remarks to the press after attending an event on Tuesday, the 18th, emphasizing his commitment to the program's continuity.

item.title: O cálculo de Davi Alcolumbre ao se reaproximar de Lula
item.description: Davi Alcolumbre is seeking to reapproach Lula to increase his chances of retaining the Senate presidency, amid declining support among Bolsonarists. According to political scientist Márcio Coimbra, the move is pragmatic, aiming to offset his loss of Bolsonarist backing by securing support from the PT base, particularly as government-backed proposals such as the end of the 6x1 work schedule and the Security PEC advance in the Senate.

item.title: Ação de Bolsonaro contra Janones entra na reta final para julgamento
item.description: Judge Giordano Resende Costa of the TJDFT has closed the evidentiary phase of the lawsuit filed by former President Jair Bolsonaro against federal deputy André Janones, over a video in which Janones accused Bolsonaro of lying about his health to secure house arrest. The case now proceeds to the final phase, where a sentence will be determined. Bolsonaro has been under house arrest since March 27, authorized by STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: TSE reúne ministros para debater uso de IA nas eleições
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) convened all its ministers on Tuesday, the 18th, to discuss the legal challenges arising from the use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns. Convened by Court President Kassio Nunes Marques, the meeting aimed to gather the positions of the tribunal's members on the issue, without any deliberation or decision being made.

item.title: Marcola recebeu contrato de venda de canabidiol de lobista, diz PF
item.description: The Federal Police found a WhatsApp message showing that Marcola, former chief of staff to President Lula, received a contract model for cannabidiol-based medication sales to the Health Ministry from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, intended to bypass public bidding. Marcola confirmed receiving the document but denied forwarding it, stating the R$ 249,000 he received were private loans already repaid. The investigation links Luchsinger to a R$ 1.5 million scheme involving Lulinha and 'Careca do INSS' to facilitate federal contracts, amid ongoing probes into INSS pension fraud.

item.title: TSE homologa desistência do PT em ação sobre recálculo do fundo eleitoral
item.description: The TSE homologated the PT's withdrawal from a lawsuit seeking to recalculate the electoral fund for 2026, extinguishing the case without ruling on the merits. The dispute centered on whether 69 or 68 federal deputies should be used as the basis for the fund's distribution, following the cassation of João Catunda. The withdrawal removes the block on disbursing the 48% of the electoral fund tied to bancada composition, allowing funds to be released to all parties.

item.title: Condenado por assassinato no Maranhão disse que tinha reuniões com governador em palácio
item.description: Gilbson Júnior, convicted of murder in São Luís, claimed in a PF deposition that he frequented the Palácio dos Leões, had a garage spot there, and delivered money to Governor Carlos Brandão and his nephew Daniel Brandão. The governor denied the allegations, stating the parking spot has been occupied by a generator for six years and that he never had any relationship with the convicted killer. The case is before the STF under Justice Flávio Dino’s rapporteurship, and Daniel Brandão’s removal from the state audit court is tied to investigations into alleged kickbacks.

item.title: Caiado ataca administração de Lula: "É um governo de ladrões"
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate for the PSD, attacked the Lula government on Tuesday (Aug 18), calling it a 'government of thieves' for allegedly shifting public debt costs onto the population. He accused the administration of using economic measures to 'deceive and numb' voters ahead of the elections and called for strong societal rejection of what he described as an 'abominable' situation. Caiado also stated that specific spending cuts cannot be outlined without first assessing the true scale of the fiscal imbalance.

item.title: Caiado diz que eleitores de esquerda “absorvem a corrupção”
item.description: Presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) claimed that left-wing voters 'absorb corruption calmly' and are resistant to corruption allegations, criticizing the PT and its supporters at an event hosted by FPN and IUB. He argued the 2026 election will feature competing national projects and stressed the need for moral authority in candidates, lamenting that polarization blocks discussion of violence and the economy. Caiado also called for reforming Executive-Legislative-Judicial relations, proposed domestic terrorism legislation, expansion of maximum-security prisons, and enhanced international cooperation against organized crime.

item.title: TSE diz que reunião entre ministros sobre inteligência artificial foi "produtiva" e servirá para orientar futuros julgamentos
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques met with the other ministers to discuss the use of artificial intelligence in electoral propaganda, describing the meeting as productive and stating it will guide future rulings. Although no consensus or specific parameters were disclosed, the Court is already showing a tendency toward stricter application of deepfake bans, as seen in ongoing virtual plenary judgments. The most significant case involves the use of AI to replicate the image and voice of Jair Bolsonaro in a video from the convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy.

item.title: Após greve da CPTM, Alesp aprova absorção de funcionários em concessões
item.description: São Paulo's Legislative Assembly (Alesp) approved a bill allowing the transfer of CPTM employees to other public entities following the privatization of lines 10-Turquesa, 11-Coral, 12-Safira and 13-Jade, ending a two-day strike that began on August 4. The bill, authored by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, awaits his sanction, but the railroad workers' union remains on strike alert, demanding full implementation of the agreement, including job absorption for employees of Line 10-Turquesa, still under state management.

item.title: Tarcísio brinca que Lula pode “carimbar estrelas” em obras de SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas joked that President Lula’s proposal to place red PT stars on joint projects, such as the Santos Tunnel, would not hinder their execution. He stressed that completing infrastructure is the priority, regardless of political visibility, and said Lula agreed with his pragmatic view that ideology should be replaced by problem-solving.

item.title: Tarcísio x Haddad: pesquisa Real Time Big Data mostra disputa em São Paulo
item.description: The Real Time Big Data poll will test spontaneous and stimulated voting intention for São Paulo governor with seven candidates, including a simulated runoff between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad. It will also measure rejection, vote potential, and the two Senate seats with 15 candidates. Results are set for release on August 24.

item.title: Caiado diz que manterá Bolsa Família, mas cobra mobilidade social
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated he will maintain the Bolsa Família as a state policy but criticized its low social mobility, noting only 2.9% of people escaped poverty to enter the upper middle class in 20 years of PT governance. He argued that investments in education, crime reduction, and narcotrafficking combat are necessary to promote population emancipation.

item.title: Lula faz apelo a Alcolumbre e Motta pelo fim da “taxa das blusinhas”
item.description: President Lula appealed to Congress to approve the provisional measure that would eliminate the 20% import tax on international purchases under US$ 50, known as the 'blusinhas tax'. He expressed optimism about the measure's approval, stating it would lower costs for Brazilian consumers. The video was released on Tuesday, March 18, and specifically addressed Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco and Chamber President Arthur Lira, despite mentioning Alcolumbre and Motta, who do not currently hold those positions.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio diz que manterá Petrobras estatal
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign coordinator, Senator Rogério Marinho, stated that a potential government would evaluate state-owned companies but has no plan to privatize Petrobras, calling it strategic. He added that the tax reform would be reviewed in the first six months to correct 'distortions', particularly the estimated 28% VAT rate, deemed unfeasible for commerce and services. Vice-presidential candidate Alfredo Gaspar pledged public spending cuts and prioritized security, proposing 500,000 new prison spots and five new federal penitentiaries.

item.title: Ex-ministro de Bolsonaro reforça campanha de Flávio
item.description: Former minister Adolfo Sachsida, an economist and lawyer who served in Jair Bolsonaro’s government, has joined the presidential campaign of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). His role will focus on organizing and presenting Flávio’s economic proposals to business leaders, investors, and productive sectors. The move aims to strengthen the campaign’s economic credibility.

item.title: Ex-FAB: Estivemos muito perto da ruptura institucional no governo Bolsonaro
item.description: Carlos de Almeida Baptista Júnior, former commander of the Brazilian Air Force, stated that Brazil was 'very close' to an institutional rupture during Jair Bolsonaro's government. He noted that the threat emerged in moments of tension between the branches of government, particularly around challenges to elections and the Constitution. The remark was made in an interview with UOL Entrevista.

item.title: Prender criminosos é “enxugar gelo”, diz Tarcísio
item.description: São Paulo governor and re-election candidate Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) said arresting criminals without effective punishment is like 'mopping ice', criticizing the release of suspects in custody hearings. He cited a case where four individuals responsible for kidnapping an elderly couple were freed after arrest, stressing that recidivism must be punished to avoid losing the 'war' on crime. Tarcísio clarified he does not support mass incarceration, but rather measures targeting habitual offending.

item.title: TRE-SP mantém multa contra Lula por pedido de voto para Tebet e Marina
item.description: São Paulo's Regional Electoral Court (TRE-SP) upheld a R$ 15,000 fine against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for premature electioneering, after he urged voters to support pre-candidates Simone Tebet and Marina Silva during a May speech broadcast on his YouTube channel. The court ruled that, despite not explicitly mentioning the 2026 elections or the Senate seat, Lula’s direct naming of the two candidates and explicit request for votes constituted illegal early campaigning, dismissing defense claims that the phrase 'one day' or lack of explicit electoral references negated the violation.

item.title: Bancos não querem “fazer o L” em 2026, diz Daniella Marques
item.description: Daniella Marques, economic coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign, warned that banks don’t want to 'do the L' in 2026, signaling lack of support for President Lula due to credit collapse risks without economic model change. She advocates for fiscal arcabouço reform, debt-to-GDP reduction, and public administration streamlining, including ministry cuts and tax reform. Despite being considered as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro, her candidacy was blocked by Republicanos’ neutrality, which selected Alfredo Gaspar instead.

item.title: Caiado anuncia Afif para ministério de pequenos negócios
item.description: Presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) announced that businessman Guilherme Afif Domingos accepted an invitation to lead a ministry dedicated to micro, small, and medium enterprises in a potential government. Afif would serve as the "voice" of small businesses in the federal administration. Caiado described the sector as "overwhelmed" with an "exposed fracture" and "arterial bleeding," and accused the federal government of promoting loan sharking against workers.

item.title: O Brasil da castração química não quer saber do diesel caro ou dos juros nos EUA
item.description: The text critiques Brazil’s political agenda, arguing that pressing issues like diesel costs and U.S. interest rates are being drowned out by sensationalist debates such as chemical castration, mass incarceration of teenagers, and street-level phone theft. It suggests a deliberate shift from structural problems to emotionally charged but low-impact topics.

item.title: Pesquisa para presidente 2026: veja últimos números atualizados
item.description: August polls show President Lula (PT) leading in first-round voting intentions for the 2026 presidential election. In potential runoff scenarios, tight races are projected against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

item.title: Campanha de Flávio quer mudar reforma tributária, mas não detalha como baixar IVA
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign coordinator, Senator Rogério Marinho, stated that they aim to revisit the tax reform within four to six months if elected, but did not specify how they would reduce the VAT. The proposal seeks to adjust the current reform, though it lacks clarity on mechanisms to lower the tax burden.

item.title: Lula diz estar convencido de que Motta e Alcolumbre vão votar fim da taxa das blusinhas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) stated in a video distributed by his campaign team on Tuesday (18) that he is confident that the presidents of the Chamber of Deputies, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), and the Senate, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), will vote to repeal the so-called 'blusinhas tax'. The remark was made in a recording shared with the press, reinforcing political pressure to end the import duty on low-value goods.

item.title: Como está a relação de Lula e Alcolumbre, segundo aliado do senador
item.description: Amapá Governor Clécio Luís described the relationship between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Davi Alcolumbre as being at its best, emphasizing Alcolumbre’s role as a pacifier and supporter of the federal government. He noted that the senator seeks consensus and helps resolve crises, citing his work on the Transition PEC and their joint visit to Amapá to announce Petrobras’ oil discovery in the Foz do Amazonas basin.

item.title: Manifesto por José Dirceu reúne classe artística e lideranças políticas
item.description: A manifesto supporting José Dirceu’s pre-candidacy for the Chamber of Deputies from São Paulo gathered signatures from artists, intellectuals, economists, and political leaders, including Alessandra Negrini, Gilberto Gil, and José Sarney. Published by O Antagonista, the document reflects broad backing from national cultural and political figures for his attempt to return to Congress.
